source.title: From Bytes to Ideas: Language Modeling with Autoregressive U-Nets
source.authors: Mathurin Videau; Badr Youbi Idrissi; A. Leite; M. Schoenauer; Olivier Teytaud; D. Lopez-Paz

record.file_problem: None noted; the supplied text includes the main paper and appendices. Some appendix tables are flattened, but that does not prevent reading the scaling-figure discussion.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across compute scales and reports how it changes, using task accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper does not report held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling curves or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation sweep. It reports downstream accuracy over compute in Figure 3; those results are recorded below. Hyperparameter-sweep results and comparisons in other tables do not directly measure the versions at issue.
record.test_reason: An architecture paper, not a scaling-law test. Figure 3 does report downstream accuracy over 1e19–1e22 FLOPs for a BPE Transformer and byte-level AU-Net. The text says most tasks follow a sigmoid: near chance at low compute, then rapid improvement, then a plateau. That is a weak, qualitative new-setting result on V6. No predictive fit is tested, and loss curves are not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' main point is that AU-Net matches strong BPE baselines at controlled compute, and that deeper hierarchies show promising trends. On scaling: downstream tasks mostly follow a sigmoid in compute. AU-Net 3 catches up on TQA at 1e22. Both AU-Net variants stay behind on MMLU and GSM8K, where improvement starts later. The authors attribute weak GSM8K results partly to little math data in DCLM.
record.recipe_differences: The paper sweeps compute and reports downstream task accuracy, rather than fitting held-out pretraining-loss power laws or measuring compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. It also fits architecture-specific batch-size and learning-rate scaling formulas.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported downstream scaling behavior varies by task and AU-Net stage count; the paper notes later improvement on MMLU and GSM8K, and a TQA catch-up only for AU-Net 3 at 1e22 FLOPs.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal batch size and learning rate, fitted on 25M–500M sweeps, follow power laws in compute. The exponents differ between AU-Net (BSZ 0.321) and BPE (BSZ 0.231). These formulas are used to set hyperparameters up to 1e22 FLOPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal hyperparameters follow power laws in compute that are architecture- and tokenization-specific, and they extrapolate to larger runs.

record.problems: The claim-relevant Figure 3 values are only shown graphically, without numerical values in the text; no uncertainty intervals are stated for that figure. The study measures downstream accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss and does not fit a predictive downstream scaling function.
record.rows_left_out: None. The claim-relevant Figure 3 task curves are recorded as separate figure-only rows for each AU-Net stage count and task.

untested.parts: No held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute is reported.
Loss extrapolation is not tested. Only learning-rate and batch-size formulas are extrapolated.
No compute-optimal parameter/token sweep. The data-to-model ratio is fixed.
There is a layer-allocation ablation, but only on downstream accuracy, not loss at fixed parameter count.
Untested: prediction of large-run downstream scores from fits on small runs, and downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss.
Fit-dependence of loss exponents or of the compute-optimal split is not examined.

missing.what: BPE baseline downstream accuracy versus compute, with no row for the baseline's own scaling curves.
Statement that most tasks follow a sigmoid pattern: near chance, then rapid improvement, then a plateau.

record.verdict_notes: The record's rows framed state as AU-Net versus BPE parity, which compares the study's own method with others. I re-anchored them to whether accuracy rises with compute. All Figure 3 values are figure only, so the evidence for V6 is qualitative.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No test of predictions from power-law fits on small runs against much larger runs.
No loss-minimising parameter/token allocation sweep at fixed compute.
No comparison of held-out loss across depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
The experiments concern text language modeling; the paper does not test the stated other modalities or training regimes.
The paper reports downstream accuracy versus compute, not downstream performance versus pretraining loss, and does not fit a quantitative predictive law to these downstream results.

The paper gives architecture-specific learning-rate and batch-size formulas, but does not test whether published loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations disagree due to setup or fitting choices, or whether loss curves bend away from a power law.

relationships.condition: BPE baseline and AU-Net on Hellaswag, ARC Easy, NQ and TQA (AU-Net 3), 1e19–1e22 FLOPs
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with compute per Figure 3 and its text (r1–r6, r8). The rise is qualitative and no predictive fit is given.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased with compute on the tested benchmarks for both BPE and AU-Net, without a fitted predictive relationship.

relationships.condition: MMLU and GSM8K, and the curve shape across tasks
relationships.reason: Improvement follows a sigmoid, near chance at low compute. Its onset shifts later for AU-Net on MMLU and GSM8K, so the onset depends on architecture (r9–r12; sigmoid statement from text).
relationships.display_finding: Scores remained near chance at low compute, with MMLU and GSM8K improvement beginning later for AU-Net.
